content:
Apple launched the next-generation M6 chip this week in the new Mac mini, but several more products are set to upgrade to M6 soon. Here's the rumored timeline for M6 Macs and iPads.

Fall 2026: MacBook Pro and iMac

Apple is reportedly set to release two more M6-equipped Macs this fall (likely October):

  • MacBook Pro
  • iMac

The MacBook Pro will only be a 14-inch base model. According to Mark Gurman, Apple will skip the M6 Pro and Max variants. So only the entry-level MacBook Pro will get M6, with the next batch of Pro-tier chips not arriving until the M7 Pro and M7 Max in 2027.

Apple's new iMac is expected to see little change beyond the M6 chip, with the only rumored upgrade being some new colors. But going from M4 to M6 still makes the new model worth upgrading to.

Worth noting is that the rumored MacBook Ultra is not on the list. It's expected to launch this fall, but with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips rather than M6.

Spring 2027: iPad Pro and MacBook Air

The first products reportedly set to upgrade to M6 in 2027 are:

  • iPad Pro
  • MacBook Air

Apple last updated the iPad Pro in fall 2025, when it jumped to the M5 chip. With a rumored spring 2027 refresh, the device will maintain its typical 18-month upgrade cycle.

Beyond the M6 chip upgrade, Apple's new iPad Pro is reportedly set to include a vapor chamber for improved thermal management—a design that could boost sustained performance on this ultra-thin device.

The M6-equipped MacBook Air is expected to launch around the same time as the iPad Pro. A window between February and April is possible, but based on Apple's track record, March is the safest bet.

Beyond the chip upgrade, rumors about the new MacBook Air are sparse. It's expected to carry over the same design as the M5 model. Reports suggest an OLED upgrade won't arrive until at least 2028, so the display will very likely remain unchanged.

One potential benefit of M6 for the iPad Pro and MacBook Air could be improved battery life. Apple says the 2-nanometer process used in M6 delivers "a major leap in performance and energy efficiency."

Which of these upcoming M6 products are you planning to upgrade to, and why? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
